ArkEngine and ArkClient define their own systems and can evolve together without being restricted by a third-party legacy codebase. # Arkengine

A typed asyncio Open Tibia server engine speaking protocol **8.60**, built as a
ground-up rewrite of a PyOT-derived engine. Milestone 1 ("walking skeleton"):
log in with OTClient, see the real map, walk around, see other players, chat,
with positions persisted.

## Architecture in one paragraph

A single asyncio process runs a fixed **20 Hz world tick** (`world/clock.py`).
The network layer (`net/`) decodes length-prefixed, adler32-checksummed,
XTEA-encrypted frames into typed commands appended to the world inbox; the
`World` (`world/world.py`) drains the inbox each tick, advances movement,
runs tick-scheduled tasks, and flushes one batched TCP write per session.
Content scripts register hooks with explicit imports and decorators
(`arkengine.scripting`) — nothing is injected into builtins. Persistence is
SQLAlchemy Core + Alembic (SQLite for dev, MySQL/Postgres by config), with
argon2id passwords and background save tasks that never block the tick.
The map subsystem (`world/map/`) hides behind narrow Protocols so a Rust
crate can replace the tile store, map-description serializer, pathfinder,
and frame codec later (milestone 4) without touching callers.

**New here? Read [docs/getting-started.md](docs/getting-started.md)** — a
zero-knowledge walkthrough from install to logged in. The full documentation
index (setup, in-game commands, combat/spells, running a server, content
authoring, and the wire protocol) is [docs/README.md](docs/README.md).

## Quick start

```bash
uv venv .venv && uv pip install -p .venv/bin/python -e ".[dev]"

# a small playable map ships in data/map-edited/ and is the default —
# nothing to copy to boot. (The full 2000x2000 world's .sec sectors are not
# in git; copy them into data/map/ and set ARKENGINE_PATHS_MAP_DIR=data/map
# to use it. See docs/getting-started.md.)

# create an account + character (applies DB migrations first)
.venv/bin/python tools/create_account.py myaccount mypassword --character Hero

# run the serve

# Arkengine

[](#arkengine)

A typed asyncio Open Tibia server engine speaking protocol **8.60**, built as a ground-up rewrite of a PyOT-derived engine. Milestone 1 ("walking skeleton"): log in with OTClient, see the real map, walk around, see other players, chat, with positions persisted.

## Architecture in one paragraph

[](#architecture-in-one-paragraph)

A single asyncio process runs a fixed **20 Hz world tick** (`world/clock.py`). The network layer (`net/`) decodes length-prefixed, adler32-checksummed, XTEA-encrypted frames into typed commands appended to the world inbox; the `World` (`world/world.py`) drains the inbox each tick, advances movement, runs tick-scheduled tasks, and flushes one batched TCP write per session. Content scripts register hooks with explicit imports and decorators (`arkengine.scripting`) — nothing is injected into builtins. Persistence is SQLAlchemy Core + Alembic (SQLite for dev, MySQL/Postgres by config), with argon2id passwords and background save tasks that never block the tick. The map subsystem (`world/map/`) hides behind narrow Protocols so a Rust crate can replace the tile store, map-description serializer, pathfinder, and frame codec later (milestone 4) without touching callers.

**New here? Read [docs/getting-started.md](/unbridledpc/arkenengine/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md)** — a zero-knowledge walkthrough from install to logged in. The full documentation index (setup, in-game commands, combat/spells, running a server, content authoring, and the wire protocol) is [docs/README.md](/unbridledpc/arkenengine/blob/main/docs/README.md).

## Quick start

[](#quick-start)

uv venv .venv && uv pip install -p .venv/bin/python -e ".\[dev\]"

# a small playable map ships in data/map-edited/ and is the default —
# nothing to copy to boot. (The full 2000x2000 world's .sec sectors are not
# in git; copy them into data/map/ and set ARKENGINE\_PATHS\_MAP\_DIR=data/map
# to use it. See docs/getting-started.md.)

# create an account + character (applies DB migrations first)
.venv/bin/python tools/create\_account.py myaccount mypassword --character Hero

# run the server (login :7171, game :7172)
.venv/bin/python -m arkengine

Point an 8.60-capable client (e.g. mehah OTClient) at `127.0.0.1:7171`, protocol/client version **8.60**. The bundled OTClient hardcodes the standard OTServ RSA key this server uses.

Config lives in `config/default.toml`; override in `config/local.toml` (gitignored) or `ARKENGINE_<SECTION>_<KEY>` env vars (e.g. `ARKENGINE_DB_URL`, `ARKENGINE_SERVER_ADVERTISE_HOST` for LAN play).

## Content scripts

[](#content-scripts)

Drop Python files under `data/scripts/`:

from arkengine.scripting import TalkContext, on\_talk

@on\_talk("!pos")
def report\_position(ctx: TalkContext) \-> bool:
    p \= ctx.player.position
    ctx.player\_message(f"You are at ({p.x}, {p.y}, {p.z}).")
    return False  \# consume; don't broadcast the say

Hooks: `on_startup`, `on_shutdown`, `on_login`, `on_logout`, `on_talk(word, match="exact"|"first_word")`, `on_walk_on(item_id)`, `on_walk_off(item_id)`. Handlers may be `async def`. Bad signatures fail at boot, not at runtime.

## Verification

[](#verification)

tools/check.sh                     # ruff + pyright (strict) + pytest
.venv/bin/python tools/smoke.py --map-only   # parse all real map sectors
.venv/bin/python tools/smoke.py    # boot real server, drive two headless bots

The integration tests run a real server on ephemeral ports and drive it with a headless 8.60 bot client (`tests/bot/client.py`) that implements its own framing and parsing, so server-side codec bugs cannot cancel themselves out.

## Roadmap

[](#roadmap)

-   **M2** — DONE (v0.2.0-m2): items & interaction — inventory/equipment, move with stack merge/split, containers (nested, multi-viewer), use items, stairs/holes/ ladders/teleports, rotate, on\_use/on\_use\_with hooks, inventory persistence
-   **M3** — DONE (v0.3.0-m3 + follow-ups): monsters & combat — legacy genMonster files run as-is, lazy spawns, chase AI, melee, corpse/loot/exp, death respawn, skills with classic advancement, food/regeneration, item rarity (5 tiers, per-drop rolls), extended-opcode channel + client tooltip module
-   **M4** — Rust hot paths (PyO3): tile store, map describer, A\*, frame codec + `tools/load.py` bot swarm for capacity measurement
-   **M5** — protocol breadth (more client versions), NPCs, spells, channels, houses

## Website

[](#website)

`.venv/bin/uvicorn --factory arkengine.web.main:create_app --port 8080` — registration, character creation, highscores (docs/website.md). Admin panel is phase 2.

## Provenance

[](#provenance)

Data (map sectors, `items.json`) and the wire-format knowledge were extracted from the legacy nexPy/PyOT engine; the code is a clean rewrite. See `docs/protocol-860.md` for the file:line-verified protocol spec.

Findings:
- Actual browser open-world action game: "Mend the Frayed Vale, fight the Unravelled and climb the Loomspire" with dodge slow-mo, parry-punish, Knotguard shields vs heavy cleave, spindle AoE, waystone travel, Emberpods, Loomhulk weak point, Lash vs Shuttlewings.
- Playable URL is the site itself (canvas + module client shell), though headless load ended in "Arkenfall could not start" — playability/performance unverified.
- No verified GitHub repo: `unbridledpc/arkenengine` search hit is an unrelated Open Tibia 8.60 engine; `repository_url: null`. No explicit engine/tech or project-source model attribution; `technologies: []`, `creation_models: []`. `gh api` unavailable (no GH_TOKEN, core rate-limited to 0), used public REST/page fetches.
- Inspected 3 images: `loading/art-03.webp` (hero sprint), `loading/art-04.webp` (bridge), `og.png` (promo banner, discounted). Screenshot score 78 — above moorestech 76 / Emberwake-Kart 70s on polish, capped as curated art with no HUD.
- Controls all `unknown`; player modes 1 / single-player from single-protagonist frames + solo objective language.
- No catalog match (66 games checked), `catalog_slug: null`. Rating 58 — above Emberwake 53 / DRIFTWING 52 / Kart Royale 50 on scope/visuals, below Meridian Wake 60 / moorestech 64 on verified systems; far from AAA with boot failure and source gaps.
